title: Change for a Dollar
statement: In how many ways can you make $100$ cents using pennies, nickels, dimes and quarters (1, 5, 10, 25 cents)? Order doesn't matter.
insight: Fix the largest coins first: for each choice of quarters and dimes, the nickel count is free and pennies fill the rest, so count nickel options in closed form.
redHerring: Counting ordered sequences of coins, which overcounts.
hints: Pennies can always fill the rest, so they never constrain anything.
For a remaining amount $r$ after quarters and dimes, how many choices of nickels are there?
That is $\lfloor r/5\rfloor + 1$. Sum over quarters $q$ and dimes $d$.
